purpose: measure how much of the compositional error is source shift, with training-set size controlled, for the controls and for every v4 row that passes its gate
pairs: every (inner fold, source s) pair that is ablatable (held-out crops and diseases stay covered) and has >= 10 evaluation images (novel-source seen-val images of s, or unseen-val images of s); 49 pairs on benchmark_v3 (artifacts: v4/feasibility_20261114/source_feasibility.json)

arms.source_ablated: all fitting images of s removed (research_r2.candidates.derive_fold keeps the v3 candidate policy)
arms.size_matched_random: 3 draws; the same NUMBER of fitting images removed from other sources, composition-stratified in proportion to each composition's other-source count, never emptying a composition; seeds 0, 1, 2

outcomes.novel_source_seen_top1: seen-val images of s whose composition keeps fitting images from another source, at gamma 0 and at the row's pooled inner gamma
outcomes.margin_shift: mean change of d = best_fitting - best_heldout score
outcomes.source_effect: source_ablated minus mean(size_matched_random); this is the size-controlled source effect

learning_curve: composition-stratified fitting fractions 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (3 draws each, seeds 0-2): H_bal at LOFO gamma and pooled-oracle gamma, to separate size from source
inference: pairs are clustered: the shared global seen holdout makes the same images recur across folds. Report unique images/compositions/sources, and a cluster bootstrap over sources (2,000 resamples, seed 0) for the mean source_effect. Not a gate.
status: diagnostic, reported for every measured row; no selection uses it
